messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "The quiet has gone too quiet — even the usual whispers have stopped. I’m starting to think we’re not waiting for a change anymore, just the moment it stops pretending to hold."
Sender 2: "The pharmacy’s running low on basics again — just like last winter, when things started getting tense. I’ve been keeping extra meds on hand, and I’d suggest you do the same."
Sender 3: "The quiet is louder than noise — things are shifting beneath the surface, and the usual signals are all out of sync. Keep your ears open, but your mouth closed."
Sender 4: "The quiet’s getting louder — things are fraying at the seams, and everyone I talk to now assumes it’s only a matter of time. Keep your lines clear, and for now, just stay close."
Sender 5: "Just got word from the clinic — they’ve been stocking extra supplies, and the usual quiet’s gone. Things feel… loose. Not panic, not yet — more like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see who blinks first. Be careful what you say."
Sender 6: "The city’s running on fumes — garbage piles up, meetings get canceled, and people are acting like the storm’s already passed. Doesn’t feel like panic, just quiet. Something’s shifting, and I don’t think it’s just me."
Sender 7: "The streets feel different — kids are chanting, but the shops are full and the trains run on time. Whatever’s coming, it’s not chaos yet. Just… waiting."
Sender 8: "The power’s starting to crack — not with noise, but with silence. The usual signals are off, and people are talking, even quietly. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our mouths shut."
Sender 9: "Just got word from a trusted source — the usual routines are breaking down quietly. Been thinking about how to handle the winter supplies, in case things get... unpredictable. Keep your channels open, but stay light on the details."
Sender 10: "The air’s changed — you can feel it in the way people talk now, even the quiet ones. Just keep your head down, watch the roads, and don’t trust a single official announcement."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
